overall_reason: The page's one picture, the nightly-run table in the hero, shows the product's own reconciliation state with numbers that check out; the rest of the page carries no imagery to fault.

score.reason: T-ILLUSTRATION-READ and T-DELETE-PICTURE pass on the hero reconciliation table, with one gap: description cells wrap and make row heights uneven (IMG-007).

findings.title: A product illustration is built to be read
findings.where: hero reconciliation table, Description column, about x 830 to 970 and y 415 to 670 of the 1440 image
findings.evidence: In the hero table the Description column is about 130px wide, so 'Northbeam Ltd, INV-2207' and 'Arden & Co, INV-2199' break onto two lines while the other three rows stay on one. The five rows end up at two heights, and the invoice numbers split from the company names.
findings.before: A narrow Description column with two wrapped rows.
findings.after: Widen the Description column by about 40px (take it from the Amount gutter) or shorten the entries to 'Northbeam, INV-2207', so every row sits on one line.
findings.why: A reconciliation table is read row by row; uneven rows make the matched and flagged lines harder to scan in the one picture that shows the product.

strengths: The hero table shows a telling state, not an empty one: 1,286 lines matched, 2 flagged, two coloured flag rows, and a footer note whose £13.40 equals the gap between the bank's -1,312.40 and the ledger's 1,299.00 for Harlow Supplies.
The page adds no mood pictures, stock people, packs or gradient art; the before-and-after bars in section 4 are plain geometry tied to stated figures.
One small icon vocabulary: thin check marks in the pricing lists and plain dots on the timeline.
not_investigated: image-only item: natural sizes, hosts, file names, alt text, density, crops at 375 and the sweep's per-element hits (fake_people, img_alt, mixed_icons, emoji_icons, icon_tile, gradient, glow, performance) were not captured; T-IMAGE-SIZE and T-CROP-375 were judged only from what the one image shows
the whole artifact is one screenshot, so it is one sample; confidence is medium at most
licences and credits: the capture cannot see licences
menus, carousels, tabs, hover states and lazy content: no interaction was captured
art direction at other widths: only one width exists
T-CAPTURE-READ: no product capture; the hero table is an illustration, judged with T-ILLUSTRATION-READ (C48)
T-TEXT-ON-IMAGE: no text over a picture

the hero table's header reads 'Tue 14 Oct' with no year; if the run is meant to be 2026 (the footer says 2026), 14 October 2026 is a Wednesday. Not raised as a finding because the table states no year
the 8.5 days to 2.5 days close-time claim under the bars is an integrity question for lens-integrity
